extracted.intended_audience: academics and researchers asked to peer review manuscripts (particularly early-career reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for researchers conducting peer review of academic papers: how to evaluate manuscripts, write clear constructive reports, avoid bias, and interact appropriately with editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Detailed and Clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviews are supposed to be in-depth critical analyses — "It's not Amazon — peer reviews are supposed to be in-depth critical analyses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a detailed, clear report that helps authors improve. Reviews should be "clear, professional, useful" (Edd Pitt). Provide substantive critique rather than brief or superficial comments; aim for depth and clarity so authors understand issues and how to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Openness to New Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not dismiss novel approaches — reviewers should be open to different perspectives and innovative reworkings of established concepts. "New insights are the lifeblood of academic fields."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reflexively rejecting work that uses unfamiliar methods or reframes issues. Evaluate the potential contribution on its own terms and consider whether the novelty advances the field rather than rejecting it for being unconventional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice Constructive Criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine critique with genuine praise so authors know "what they can relax about and where they need to focus."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance negative feedback with recognition of strengths. Make criticisms actionable (specific suggestions for improvement), and highlight what is working well to guide authors' revision priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper "makes a contribution towards moving the field forward," independent of personal agreement; guard against confirmation bias and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the manuscript's contribution and evidence rather than the author's views. Disclose and avoid hidden conflicts of interest. Be self-aware about biases and ensure evaluation criteria are applied consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Unnecessary Nitpicking
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not comment on minor typos unless grammar significantly impairs comprehension; avoid focusing on trivial issues at the expense of substantive critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize substantive problems (conceptual, methodological, interpretive) over minor copy-editing. Note only those language/format issues that hinder understanding; leave routine copy-editing to journal editors or the copyedit stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the Editor's Decision Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept/reject recommendations belong solely to editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide your assessment and, if requested, a recommendation, but do not presume to make the final decision. Frame recommendations as your informed opinion to assist the editor rather than an authoritative verdict.
